memory_candidates.content: A gate check that reports multiple labelled sub-states through one display-capped loop (e.g. a validator with missing_key/null_value/empty_array findings, all WARN, capped at the first N by sort order) cannot have a subset of those sub-states promoted to FAIL without also exempting the FAIL findings from the display cap. Otherwise a FAIL-level finding that sorts past the cap (likely once the still-WARN population outnumbers the cap) prints no FAIL line and the promotion silently regresses to cosmetic -- exit code stays 0 despite the exact condition the promotion was meant to block. The fix: split the emission loop by level (FAIL findings untruncated, WARN findings capped), and recompute any '...and N more' arithmetic against the WARN population only. Verify the fix is load-bearing (not vacuous) by disabling the exemption in a scratch copy and confirming a fixture with a FAIL finding deliberately sorting past the cap starts missing its specific per-finding assertion -- checking only the aggregate line or the overall exit code is not sufficient, since both can still fire for unrelated reasons (an aggregate FAIL line computed from a raw count, not the capped list; a different FAIL elsewhere in the same run).

When a plan's Scope Hypothesis predicts N existing test fixtures will break under a validator-posture change, re-run the UNMODIFIED test suite against the already-edited validator before touching any fixture, and read every failure rather than stopping once N failures are found. In this task, a change that promotes one sub-state of a multi-state check from WARN to FAIL broke a third, unanticipated fixture: a --fix/--repair-mode fixture that deliberately carries the exact shape the repair must NOT touch (a null-valued field, to prove non-mutation) -- the repair run's own exit code flips because the validation pass it runs internally now reports the promoted FAIL. The general pattern: any fixture that invokes the validator in a secondary mode (--fix, --repair, a wrapper script) over an input containing the condition being promoted is a hidden second consumer of the promoted check's exit code, easy to miss when scanning only for fixtures that test the check directly.
